newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas tight, pressures spread.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas tight, pressures spread.

text.p: Softer naphtha faced by bullish gasoline extended the pressure on the spread between light distillates, trader said on Monday.
"Gasoline is looking a bit tight.. the spread has widened so much," a trader said.
Since late last week, the spread had widened to $4.00-$5.00 per barrel, from around $2.00, traders said.
"The current tightness is because of the shutdowns in this region in March and cut backs in reformer runs," a trader said.
Singapore Refining Co started a scheduled shutdown of a 90,000 barrel-per-day crude distillation unit (CDU) on Sunday and will be down until March 21, sources said.
Mobil Singapore is planning to turn around its 280,000-bpd refinery mid-March for four to six weeks.

Problems to restart the 83,000-bpd hydrocracker at Indonesia's Exor-1 refinery at Balongan, and the ensuing shutdown of the 125,000-bpd CDU, was also causing some demand for low-octane gasoline, traders said.
They said up to half a million barrels were being imported into Indonesia in March.

In the Singapore fob market, the low 92-octane unleaded grade was actively talked between two Japanese trading houses, with a bid for 80,000 barrels at $27.70 per barrel, facing the seller of 50,000 barrels at $27.90, both for March 18-22 lifting. On Friday, the grade traded at $27.75 for March 17-21 lifting.
Unleaded 95-octane grade was bid by a European major at $28.20 for March 18-22.
In the medium term, traders said they were looking to Taiwan's reformate import tender for first-half April which closes Tuesday.
"It is a good indication of April,' said a trader on the tender.
"Offers should come in above $28.00 c-and-f Taiwan, although at the current high fob Singapore prices, anything below $29.00 does not look so attractive," he said.

Saudi Aramco also has an import tender closing Tuesday, for up to 1.5 million barrels of 95-octane 0.4 grammes per litre gasoline or, four 300,000-barrel cargoes for delivery to Ras Tanura in the Mideast Gulf between April 1-3, 5-7, 9-11, 14-16 and one optional cargo for April 18-20.
The tender is valid until March 12.
Traders said Saudi Aramco last sought gasoline through a term tender for the first quarter where it bought about two cargoes a month.

A source at Vietnamese state-owned Petrolimex told Reuters it bought 18,000-tonnes of 83-octane unleaded gasoline at 20-25 cents per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes on a c-and-f basis in February as one term supplier was unable to supply the cargo. The seller was a Russian oil company.
Naphtha March swaps fell by 70 cents per barrel to $22.20/$22.40 with Friday's drop in crude amid bearish sentiment as arbitrage cargoes flow in from the West, traders said.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
